grades.quote: When MXR=0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1 in Figure 67) will succeed. When MXR=1, loads from pages marked either readable or executable (R=1 or X=1) will succeed. MXR has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
grades.reason: Directly explains that MXR permits loads from execute-only pages when set, with the virtual-memory limitation.

grades.quote: Attempting to execute a load or load-reserved instruction whose effective address lies within a page without read permissions raises a load page-fault exception.

grades.quote: The `vsstatus` field MXR, which makes execute-only pages readable by explicit loads, only overrides VSstage page protection. Setting MXR at VS-level does not override guest-physical page protections. Setting MXR at HS-level, however, overrides both VS-stage and G-stage execute-only permissions.
grades.reason: Directly states that MXR enables explicit loads from execute-only pages and explains its scope under two-stage translation.
